safety_verdicts.content: The headache improves when the patient is lying down.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state that headache improves when lying down; it only notes no positional worsening / that the patient has been lying down.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether headache improves when lying down is a key positional feature that can shift the differential toward intracranial hypotension/CSF leak or other secondary causes, potentially changing urgency and workup. Omitting this may delay recognition of a potentially significant secondary headache syndrome and appropriate referral/imaging.

safety_verdicts.content: The headache has not awakened the patient from sleep.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention whether the headache has awakened the patient from sleep.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Headache awakening a patient from sleep is a common “red flag” screening item; documenting that it does not occur supports a less concerning picture. Omission can reduce the quality of safety-netting/triage decisions and may prompt unnecessary follow-up or, conversely, miss escalation triggers in documentation.
